24/7
TWEN-tee-for SEV-en
adverb / adjective (Gen X slang)
Short for "twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week." Recorded in American sports and street slang by the mid-1980s for "all the time, constantly," it spread with all-night convenience stores, ATMs, and round-the-clock services, and was nationwide by the early 1990s, later stretched to 24/7/365. The never-closed world it names arrived with cable news (CNN, 1980) and, by the late 1990s, the always-on internet.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

24/7 means all the time, without a break: "She texts him 24/7." "This job is 24/7." It began as a store sign and became a way of life — the always-open shop, the always-on news, and at last the always-on phone. The Christian observation is that only One is truly 24/7. "Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep" (Psa 121:4). God’s mercies are not rationed by business hours: "his compassions fail not. They are new every morning" (Lam 3:22-23). And He invites His people into a holy kind of constancy — "Pray without ceasing" (1Th 5:17), and the blessed man meditates in God’s law "day and night" (Psa 1:2). But here is the turn: God does not ask His creatures to be 24/7 in the way He is. He built rest into the week before there was a store to keep open. "Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God" (Exo 20:9-10). "The sabbath was made for man" (Mar 2:27). A culture that never closes is a culture trying to be God, and it exhausts its children. "It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late … for so he giveth his beloved sleep" (Psa 127:2). A father can say to a son who is grinding 24/7, or scrolling 24/7: you are not the one who keeps the world running; the Lord does. Pray always, work hard six days, and rest on the seventh, trusting the One who never sleeps.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen X slang (1980s, from "twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week") for constantly, nonstop; only God neither slumbers nor sleeps (Psa 121:4), and He built a sabbath into His creatures’ week (Exo 20:10).

24/7, adv. and adj. (Gen X slang, mid-1980s–present) All the time; constantly; around the clock. "He plays that game 24/7." "A 24/7 job."

Read "twenty-four seven"; from "twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week." Extended: 24/7/365.

Spread with all-night stores, ATMs, cable news (CNN, 1980), and the late-1990s always-on internet.

No entry in Webster 1828; the numeral shorthand is late-20th-century American slang.

Decode for parents: the world never closes; teach your children that only God is 24/7, and that He commanded us to rest.

Key Scripture

Psa 121:4 — "Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep."

Lam 3:23 — "They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."

1Th 5:17 — "Pray without ceasing."

Exo 20:10 — "But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:"

Psa 127:2 — "It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep."

Modern Corruption

24/7 is the creed of a world that never closes; Scripture reserves sleepless watchfulness for God alone and gives His creatures the gift of a weekly rest.

expand to see more

Playing God with the clock. A civilization that keeps its stores, screens, and offices open around the clock is quietly claiming an attribute that belongs to God: He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep (Psa 121:4). Men who try to match Him end up anxious and exhausted. The Psalmist calls it vain to rise early and sit up late eating the bread of sorrows (Psa 127:2); the always-on worker and the always-on teenager are proving him right every night.

Constant prayer, weekly rest. Scripture has its own 24/7: pray without ceasing (1Th 5:17), meditate day and night (Psa 1:2), mercies new every morning (Lam 3:23). But it pairs that constancy with a command to stop. The sabbath (Exo 20:10) is a weekly confession that God runs the world and we do not. A family that rests one day in seven, phones down and Bibles open, is preaching that sermon to its children.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

"Twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week" → mid-1980s sports and street slang 24/7 → 1990s nationwide → the always-on phone; Scripture: He neither slumbers nor sleeps, and giveth His beloved sleep (Psa 121:4; Psa 127:2).
